title: Dive into Time-Series Anomaly Detection: A Decade Review
authors: Boniol, P.; Liu, Q.; Huang, M.; Palpanas, T.; Paparrizos, J.
tldr: Comprehensive survey of time-series anomaly detection methods organized under a process-centric taxonomy spanning distance-based, density-based, and prediction-based approaches, with a meta-analysis of a decade of research trends.
problem_and_motivation: Time-series anomaly detection lacks a unified, process-centric taxonomy that groups methods by their detection mechanism rather than by application domain. Existing surveys focus on general-purpose anomaly detection and only briefly review time-series-specific methods. Disconnected research communities evaluate methods on different datasets and baselines, making cross-community comparison virtually impossible.
approach: Proposed a three-level process-centric taxonomy grouping all time-series anomaly detection methods into distance-based, density-based, and prediction-based families.
Introduced a four-stage anomaly detection pipeline model (pre-processing, detection, scoring, post-processing) to unify the comparison of methods.
Classified methods along dimensions of univariate vs. multivariate, and unsupervised vs. semi-supervised vs. supervised.
Conducted a meta-analysis of the literature from 1990 to 2023 tracking publication trends across method categories.
Reviewed eight major benchmarks (NAB, Yahoo, Exathlon, KDD21, TODS, TimeEval, TSB-UAD, TSB-AD) for evaluation.
Analyzed threshold-based and threshold-independent evaluation measures including AUC-ROC, AUC-PR, Range-AUC, and VUS.
Described over 80 individual algorithms with formal definitions of key concepts such as discord, matrix profile, and LOF.
findings: num: The number of proposed anomaly detection methods increased significantly after 2016, driven primarily by deep learning approaches.
num: Between 2020 and 2023, prediction-based methods (LSTM and autoencoder) represented almost 50% of newly introduced methods.
num: 65% of anomaly detection methods proposed between 1980 and 2000 were unsupervised, whereas only 50% of methods proposed between 2012 and 2018 were unsupervised.
Most methods proposed before 2016 targeted multivariate time series, but recent interest in sub-sequence detection shifted focus toward univariate methods.
No single best anomaly detector exists across all datasets; simple time-series classification baselines can improve accuracy by a factor of 2 over the best individual method for model selection.
TSB-UAD with 14,046 time series and TSB-AD with 1,070 curated datasets are the largest and most comprehensive benchmarks available.
VUS-ROC is recommended as the most robust, separable, and consistent evaluation metric for time-series anomaly detection.
Existing benchmarks have known flaws including triviality, unrealistic anomaly density, mislabeled ground truth, and run-to-failure bias.
The prediction-based anomaly detection pipeline operates under the assumption that normal data are easier to predict than anomalous data.

key_equations.explanation: KNN anomaly score aggregating distances to k nearest neighbors.
Local Outlier Factor comparing local reachability densities.
Isolation Forest anomaly score based on average path length.

definitions.definition: An ordered sequence of real-valued data points.
A single data point that deviates remarkably from the rest of the data.
A data point within the normal range globally but abnormal within its local context.
A sequence of points that collectively do not match a previously observed normal pattern.
A subsequence whose nearest neighbor distance is the largest among all subsequence nearest neighbor distances.
A metadata time series where each element is the Euclidean distance of a subsequence to its nearest neighbor.
Local Outlier Factor, a density-based anomaly score measuring how isolated a point is relative to its local neighborhood.
A tree-based anomaly detector that isolates anomalies using random recursive partitioning.
Long Short-Term Memory, a recurrent neural network architecture with gating mechanisms for learning long-range dependencies.
Variational Autoencoder, a generative model that learns a latent representation for reconstruction-based anomaly scoring.
Volume Under the Surface, a parameter-free, threshold-independent evaluation measure.
Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve.
Dynamic Time Warping, a distance measure that handles temporal misalignment.
AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average, a linear time-series forecasting model.
Hierarchical Temporal Memory, a neural architecture based on the Thousand Brains Theory.
Echo State Network, a recurrent neural network with a randomly connected hidden reservoir.
Gated Recurrent Unit, a simplified RNN gating mechanism.
Generative Adversarial Network, a framework with competing generator and discriminator networks.
Mueen's ultra-fast Algorithm for Similarity Search, an FFT-based method for computing subsequence distances.
Symbolic Aggregate Approximation, a method for discretizing time series into symbolic representations.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This survey provides the first comprehensive process-centric taxonomy of time-series anomaly detection methods, organizing over 80 algorithms into distance-based, density-based, and prediction-based families. The meta-analysis reveals that deep learning methods have dominated since 2016. The paper also reviews eight benchmarks and evaluation metrics, recommending VUS-ROC as the most robust measure.
directly_justifies: Process-centric taxonomy groups anomaly detection into distance-based, density-based, and prediction-based families.
Prediction-based methods dominate post-2016 publications at nearly 50% of new methods.
No single anomaly detector works best across all datasets.
VUS-ROC is recommended as the most robust evaluation metric.
limits: Focuses on general time-series anomaly detection, not specifically financial data.
No agreed-upon standard benchmark exists across the community.

limitations: Survey is descriptive without empirical comparison across methods.
Taxonomy categories are not mutually exclusive.
No financial datasets used in evaluation benchmarks reviewed.
